articles.title: Bessent pekar ut Lutnick för AI-läckage till Kina
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Bessent pekar ut Lutnick för AI-läckage till Kina
articles.body_text: USA:s finansminister Scott Bessent och handelsminister Howard Lutnick. Arkivbild. Bessent pekar ut Lutnick för AI-läckage till Kina Finansminister Scott Bessent pekar finger åt ministerkollegan Howard Lutnick i fråga om varför inte USA bättre lyckats stoppa utförsel av avancerade AI-chip till Kina. Frågan är kopplad till skandalen kring Nvidias tidigare vd Jensen Huang. Bessent säger till CNBC på fredagen att hans departement, bland flera i regeringen, länge har förespråkat restriktioner mot det Singaporebaserade företaget Megaspeed – som står i centrum för spioneri- och sexskandalen kring Jensen Huang. I fråga om varför inga restriktioner införts svarar Bessent att det är handelsdepartementet, under handelsminister Lutnick, som har ansvaret. Så ni får fråga dem om deras interna processer. Jensen Huang fick sparken på torsdagen, bland annat på grund av en otrohetsaffär med affärskvinnan Alice Huang, som han trots efternamnet inte är släkt med. Alice Huang har i sin tur haft starka kopplingar till Megaspeed, som bland annat ska ha importerat stora mängder teknik från Nvidia. Det ska enligt flera medieuppgifter finnas misstankar om att Alice Huang är spion, på uppdrag av Kinas regering. Howard Lutnick har enligt nyhetssajten Axios ”upprepade gånger satt sig på tvären” mot åtgärder riktade mot företag som misstänks slussa vidare Nvidias avancerade AI-chip till Kina. Enligt Scott Bessent skadar överföringen av avancerad teknik till Kina "våra fantastiska företag i AI-kapplöpningen”.

articles.title: Tinder bötfälls för brott mot EU-lagar
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Tinder bötfälls för brott mot EU-lagar
articles.body_text: Tinder har enligt en tillsynsmyndighet inte levt upp till EU:s GDPR-regler. Arkivbild. Tinders ägarbolag ska böta motsvarande 122 miljoner kronor. Dejtingappen anklagas för att inte ha levt upp till EU:s dataskyddsregler. DPC kräver att Match Group, som äger Tinder, ska börja leva upp till EU:s allmänna dataskyddsförordning GDPR. Problemet ligger i appens verktyg för att ladda ned sin personliga data, som enligt DPC inte presenterat alla uppgifter som GDPR kräver. Match Group planerar att överklaga myndighetens beslut.

articles.title: Nvidia-aktien fortsätter falla efter kaoset
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Nvidia-aktien fortsätter falla efter kaoset
articles.body_text: Nvidia-aktien fortsätter falla efter kaoset Halvledarjätten Nvidia fortsätter falla när New York-börsen öppnat sin handel. Detta efter några dagar av blodig kursslakt i kaoset kring vd:n Jensen Huangs otrohetsaffärer. Efter knappt fem minuters handel på fredagen har Nvidias aktie stigit 0,6 procent. De senaste fem handelsdagarna har en tiondel av bolagets börsvärde utraderats – innan Huang fick sparken på torsdagen på grund av flera otrohetsaffärer som uppdagats inom bara några dagar. Nvidia är fortfarande världens näst högst värderade börsbolag efter Apple. Nvidias mer direkta konkurrenter i chiptillverkningen, Broadcom och AMD – som steg rejält under Nvidias ras – faller nu i stället, 1,9 respektive 2,5 procent. Börsen i stort rör sig relativt försiktigt. Dow Jones industriindex har stigit 0,3 procent, breda S&P 500-index 0,2 och tekniktunga Nasdaqs kompositindex 0,1 procent. Microsoft – trea på den globala börsvärdeslistan – haltar i sin tur fram på börsen. Mjukvarujätten kämpar på fredagen mot tekniska problem med sina datatjänster. Aktien har fallit 1,4 procent.

articles.title: Producentpriser ökar något mindre än väntat i USA
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Producentpriser ökar något mindre än väntat i USA
articles.body_text: Rapport om producentpriserna i USA i april. Arkivbild Producentpriser ökar något mindre än väntat i USA Producentpriserna i USA steg 0,3 procent i oktober jämfört med september. I årstakt innebär det en prisökning i producentled på 6,5 procent i världens största ekonomi. Det var en något dämpad prisökning jämfört med förväntningarna. Analytiker hade i genomsnitt räknat med en ökning på 0,4 procent jämfört med september och 6,6 procent jämfört med oktober i fjol, enligt Bloomberg. Rensar man bort energi- och livsmedelspriser var ökningen av producentpriserna i oktober 0,3 procent mot månaden före och 5,0 procent jämfört med oktober i fjol – i linje med förväntningarna. Prisutvecklingen i producentled är högintressant data som en sorts inflationsindikator inför räntebeskedet från USA:s centralbank Federal Reserve (Fed) i december, där marknaden räknar med en höjd styrränta.

articles.title: IMF: Finland behöver strama åt statsfinanserna
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: IMF: Finland behöver strama åt statsfinanserna
articles.body_text: Inflationstrycket i Finland fortsätter nedåt. Arkivbild IMF: Finland behöver strama åt statsfinanserna Finland – Sveriges femte största exportmarknad – borde fokusera på hållbara statsfinanser och strama åt budgeten, enligt en rapport från Internationella valutafonden (IMF). Rådet är att från och med 2027 strama åt budgeten med 0,5 procent av BNP per år med sikte på att få bort landets stora budgetunderskott till och med 2035, enligt IMF:s rekommendationer. I första hand krävs enligt IMF:s experter flera års utgiftsminskningar, men även tillväxtstimulerande intäktsökningar. Enligt IMF har Finlands ekonomi återhämtat sig i år, men arbetslösheten är fortfarande hög och riskerar att fastna på en hög nivå. Och ungdomsarbetslösheten hotar kompetensutveckling och sysselsättningstrenderna på sikt, enligt rapporten.

articles.title: Publicistiska grunden för journalistik på TV4
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.title: Bortglömda fiskar
articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. De uppsluppna tillställningarna, före och efter konserter och föreställningar, lockar också en ny sorts publik. En av Östersjöfestivalens mest omtalade programpunkter, förutom musiken i Berwaldhallen, har varit “Bortglömda fiskar” - en oväntad kulinarisk träff med Kålrotsakademin och provsmakning av “svensk sushi”. “Gensvaret från publiken är enormt. Man vill bli överraskad”, konstaterar Emma Nyberg, exekutiv producent på Berwaldhallen. Och på frågan om vad nors och näbbgädda har att göra i ett konserthus kommer det självklara svaret snabbt: “Att äta gott och att lyssna på klassisk musik hör ihop, båda skärper och öppnar våra sinnen.”

articles.title: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption
articles.summary: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers.
articles.body_text: Microsoft has said it is "deeply sorry" for the service outage to its products, including Outlook and Teams, which has caused disruption around the world. Services were broadly recovering by Friday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after issues began. Microsoft said it was making "encouraging progress", but added it does not know when services will fully recover. The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide. Microsoft said it was a technical issue introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and not related to cyber or artificial intelligence agents. Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers. Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday. By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America. In the UK, some parts of the NHS, including GPs and hospitals, were affected , as were some schools and police forces. UK cyber minister Liz Lloyd said the incident had "limited" impact on critical frontline services such as 999 calls, and there had been no disruption to the transport network. In Canada, however, the national rail network said passengers may not be able to receive email updates about their trips, and hospitals across the country also had issues with emails. In the US, staff members from the House of Representatives told Politico it had set back an entire day of legislative work as everything was on Microsoft's Outlook. Singapore's government acknowledged some of its systems had been impacted, and in India, the outage disrupted work for many on Friday.

articles.title: Pope Leo visits the Peruvian city that has embraced him as one of its own
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.
articles.body_text: Pope Leo XIV has celebrated Mass near the Peruvian city where he made his name as a compassionate bishop who worked closely with poor and migrant communities. The ceremony was held on Friday at a park in Pimentel, about 10km (six miles) from Chiclayo in northern Peru as part of his tour of Latin America. The Vatican estimates more than 1.5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff. "Thank you for your affection, support and prayers," the Pope told followers. "Especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God's help, I am overcoming," he added, referencing the surgery he had for lung cancer which took place just weeks ago . Some of the crowd arrived 12 hours in advance to wait in vigil before the Mass began. "We spent the night praying, alongside family, excited to welcome the Pope from Chiclayo," said Isa Orderique. Many came from across Peru and even neighbouring countries to attend. Merli Cruz Guerrero, from an area near the Ecuadorean border, travelled several hours by bus to attend. She also spent the entire night waiting. Of all the events the Pope has attended so far during his visit to Peru, this felt particularly emotional. The crowd fell into a hushed silence as the pontiff's motorcade approached. They waited eagerly for his arrival despite spending long hours out in the open with the temperature pushing past 30C.

articles.title: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine
articles.summary: The fact the question of European security now features in discussions is viewed in Moscow as a victory, BBC Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg says.
articles.body_text: Russia's President Vladimir Putin says he wishes "eternal peace" for Ukraine. That is the same Russian president who ordered the full-scale invasion of Russia's neighbour nearly five years ago and who continues to reject the idea of a comprehensive ceasefire. And what, in Moscow's view, is a prerequisite for peace? The Kremlin spelt it out after talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner: "A new, long-term architecture of indivisible security and peace." Translated from Kremlin-speak, it means Moscow wants to change the security set-up of Europe in a way that benefits Russia. What Russia is pushing for is, potentially, the biggest change to European security arrangements since the end of the Cold War. The Kremlin has put back on the table its controversial proposal from December 2021 – the "draft treaties" with the US and Nato which would not only have put the brakes on the alliance's eastward enlargement by giving Moscow cast-iron guarantees that, for instance, Ukraine and Georgia would never be allowed to join, but also rolled back Nato military infrastructure from countries of central and eastern Europe which became Nato members following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. Western leaders dismissed such demands as an unacceptable Russian ultimatum. Two months later Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The "draft treaties" were put away. Now they are out of the geopolitical filing cabinet, and being quoted again by the Kremlin. What is more, Yuri Ushakov, Putin's foreign policy aide, has suggested that Moscow is about to "add certain new considerations" to its list of demands in light of Western efforts "to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia". That does not mean, of course, that Western governments will accept them. But the fact that the question of European security is featuring now in discussions on Ukraine is viewed here as a victory for Moscow.

articles.title: Chris Van Hollen to challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate leadership
articles.summary: Maryland Senator Van Hollen says "new leadership" is needed for Democrats following the party's recent midterm successes.
articles.body_text: Senator Chuck Schumer is facing a challenge to his position as US Senate majority leader from his fellow Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen, as the party prepares to take control of Congress after sweeping the midterm elections. Van Hollen, 67, said in a post on X on Thursday that Americans voted for change earlier this month and "to deliver, we need new leadership". Schumer, 75, has led Democrats in the chamber since 2017, serving as both majority and minority leader. He was first elected to the Senate in 1999. Following the midterms earlier this month, his position has come under pressure by some left-wing Democrats who see him as too moderate and part of the party establishment. Responding to the challenge, Schumer, who represents New York, said he welcomed "any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead". He added that he was "proud of what we've accomplished together" in the midterms, and he had "the votes to continue as Democratic leader". The vote on Senate leader will be held behind closed doors in early December and the winner will assume the role on 4 January, when Democrats take control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives after their midterms successes. The move by Van Hollen, who represents Maryland, marks the most significant step by a high-profile Democrat to challenge the party's existing leadership following last week's midterms victory. Announcing his plans to run in a post on X, he wrote that Americans had called on the party to "unrig an economy rigged against working people". "We should not be preserving our institutions if they are not delivering for the American people," he said at a summit in Colorado hosted by majority Democrats. "And we should be making delivering for the American people the single mission of our government, even when that means shaking things up." He added: "This country does not belong to the people who can afford to buy influence. It belongs to all of us. And it's time we govern like that." In recent years, Van Hollen has taken positions popular with those on the left of his party.

articles.title: German spies handed new powers to tackle 'hybrid threats' from abroad
articles.summary: German reforms mean foreign and domestic intelligence services will have greater powers to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage.
articles.body_text: Germany's foreign and domestic intelligence services are to be given greater powers to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage after the country's parliament, the Bundestag, approved a major overhaul of its legislation. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, who championed the bill, has called it a "reform of the century", necessary because of the increasing threats from foreign powers. But the Left Party's security spokeswoman, Clara Bünger, said Dobrindt was creating a new German secret police. The legislation gives numerous new powers to Germany's BND federal intelligence service, and its BfV domestic service, the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution. In the Bundestag, 309 MPs voted in favour of the new law on intelligence services, while 190 voted against and 71 abstained. For historical reasons, German intelligence has mainly focused on gathering information rather than acting on it. In future, German spies working for the BND, which is responsible for foreign intelligence, will be able to conduct covert operations abroad, including sabotage. This could include paralysing the servers of state-sponsored hacker groups, disrupting disinformation networks, or even disrupting supply chains for weapons. Agents for the domestic intelligence service, the BfV, will no longer to be limited to gathering information. For the first time they will be able to take protective action against property and IT systems, if specific threats are identified. That means they will be allowed to dismantle or break explosives or weapons, divert or block data flows during cyber-attacks, delete or falsify data stored for malicious purposes, and plant false information on those involved. Under certain conditions, BfV agents will also be permitted to enter homes covertly. However, the measure must always be authorised in advance. They will also be given wider powers of digital surveillance, including monitoring encrypted telecommunications and carrying out online searches. They will also be allowed to use AI-supported data analysis and biometric image matching on the internet.

articles.title: Bessent blames Lutnick's department for Nvidia chip sales to Megaspeed
articles.summary: Scott Bessent told CNBC that several government agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".
articles.body_text: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-spec AI chips, as the fallout from the Nvidia scandal widens to President Donald Trump's cabinet. Pressure is building on Lutnick from across the political spectrum to explain his department's actions. Jensen Huang was ousted as Nvidia CEO after revelations he had an affair with a businesswoman who was also allegedly a Chinese spy. Megaspeed, the firm she worked for, had been probed by US government agencies over suspicions it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China, reports said, but it is not on a list of firms US companies are prevented from working with. Bessent told CNBC several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months". "But Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added. Bessent's comments come after Lutnick was called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over the Commerce Department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips. Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Huang. Bessent said he was "frustrated" by delays in putting the company on the export control list and reports of leakage of AI chips into China. "President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s, so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, because it gives the Chinese an advantage," he said. Last year, the Commerce Department had been investigating Megaspeed over suspicions it had been smuggling some of Nvidia's advanced AI chips into China, according to the New York Times. Megaspeed has been contacted for comment. There was also pressure on the Commerce Department to add it to the list, but separate reporting in the Financial Times said the department was delaying efforts to have the cloud computing firm included.

articles.title: Aide to pro-Kremlin Ukrainian ex-PM badly hurt in Moscow car bomb
articles.summary: Sergei Zavorotny, now a journalist and commentator, was previously an adviser to Ukrainian ex-prime minister Mykola Azarov.
articles.body_text: A car bomb attack in Moscow has wounded a former adviser to Ukrainian ex-prime minister Mykola Azarov, Russia's Investigative Committee says. Sergei Zavorotny, now a journalist and commentator, was behind the wheel of his black Toyota when the explosion happened and Azarov told Russian TV his condition in hospital was "rather critical". The car bomb went off a day after a Russian colonel was killed in another explosion in St Petersburg, and both blasts are seen as part of a series of attacks on military and prominent figures linked to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Zavorotny, 72, worked as a press aide to Mykola Azarov in Kyiv until 2014. But when pro-Kremlin Ukrainian president Viktor Yanukovych was toppled from power, Azarov fled Kyiv for Russia and tried unsuccessfully to set up a government in exile. In a 2020 US Senate report on interference in the 2016 American presidential election, Zavorotny is described at the time as an SVR [Russian foreign intelligence] officer involved in influence operations. Russia's Investigative Committee said on Telegram on Friday: "Serhiy Zavorotny, a former adviser to the former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, was injured while driving a car. He was taken to one of the city hospitals, where he is receiving medical care." It added: "A set of necessary investigative actions is being carried out. A number of examinations will be appointed, including medical and explosives." According to several unconfirmed reports, Zavorotny suffered a number of serious injuries after an explosive device was detonated remotely. Russia said the car bombs are the latest in a series of attacks targeting pro-Kremlin figures. On Thursday a car bomb in the Pushkinsky District of St Petersburg killed a member of the Russian military, again after it was attached to the base of the car and detonated remotely. The man targeted in the attack is yet to be named officially, but reputable sources suggest he was a high-ranking figure in the 6th Guards Air and Air Defence Forces Army.

articles.title: Rosalía scoops historic third best album award at Latin Grammys
articles.summary: The Spanish singer is recognised for her fourth album Lux which was released last year to rave reviews.
articles.body_text: Spanish star Rosalía has made history as the first woman to win the best album award at the Latin Grammys three times, after being recognised for her project Lux. The singer took home five trophies in total, including two for her track La Perla which was named song of the year and best pop song. La Perla was also nominated for record of the year but missed out to Argentine singer Milo J's song Niño. Rosalía released Lux last year to rave reviews and collecting her award at the ceremony in Las Vegas on Thursday, she said: "To all the people who told me I wasn't good enough, or that my music was too weird, I'm thankful I didn't listen." The Barcelona-born artist then added: "Now I'm winning these prizes." Rosalía, who opened the ceremony with a performance of some of her biggest songs, was honoured with the prize for best alternative music album. She also picked up best shortform music video for her track Sauvignon Blanc. The singer had previously won best album for El Mal Querer in 2019 and Motomami in 2022 - and her third Lux is also tipped to be a favourite when nominations are announced for the Grammys next week. It was also a big night for Puerto Rican reggaeton legend Daddy Yankee, who won the person of the year award. He performed some of his best-loved tracks including Gasolina and Con Calma, and was joined on stage by rappers including LL Cool J and French Montana. Microsoft said the outage was not a cyber-security incident and was caused by a technical issue. It has apologised for the disruption. Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong. Some Microsoft 365 services have been affected by "connectivity problems" with problems reported in at least 74 countries. From late on Thursday, customers reported varying levels of access - many were unable to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps. But some users were able to use Teams, messaging and online meeting functions without issues. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe and improvement in North America. The company added that it was focused on "addressing the remaining areas of disruption" but warned "some users may still experience intermittent issues". In a later statement, the company said it was continuing to see improvements "with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels". The company attributed the ongoing outage to an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade. "We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions," it said on Friday.

articles.summary: Hall has been seeking a US visa in South Africa as other African beauty queens face similar hurdles.
articles.body_text: Miss Universe Zimbabwe Roseanna Hall and several other contestants from Africa could miss this year's competition in Puerto Rico as they race to secure a US visa. Hall is due to represent Zimbabwe at the 75th edition of the Miss Universe pageant, with the winner set to be crowned on 24 November. But she has yet to obtain a visa to travel to the US territory. "We have been back and forth, trying to get my visa approved," Hall said in a video posted on her Instagram page. Hall is not the only African contestant to be affected by the restrictions. Zambia has withdrawn its representative, Pamela Mubanga, from the competition because of US travel restrictions. Contestants began arriving in Puerto Rico on 8 November for registration, fittings and other pre-pageant activities, putting pressure on Hall, and others including the representative from South Sudan, to secure their visas. "Officially, today is the day I was supposed to be leaving for Puerto Rico for the 75th edition of Miss Universe," Hall said. Zimbabwe is among 19 countries subject to partial US travel restrictions introduced under the Presidential Proclamation 10998, which took effect on 1 January 2026. The measures suspend the issuance of visitor, student and exchange visas, as well as immigrant visas, to nationals of the affected countries. They also impose restrictions on other categories of non-immigrant visas. In a statement, the Miss Universe organization in Zambia said Mubanga's situation was a consequence of the travel restrictions rather than individual circumstances. "Unlike situations where a contestant's visa is denied due to personal circumstances, documentation or organisational challenges, Mubanga's situation is linked to the United States' presidential travel restriction affecting Zambia and other African countries," the statement read. Mubanga, 25, a registered nurse, was crowned Miss Universe Zambia on 8 October and was due to represent the country at the international pageant. The statement said five other African countries faced similar difficulties, although it did not name them.

articles.body_text: León XIV llegó al Perú este miércoles 11 de noviembre, a las 5:30 p. m., para comenzar una visita que combinará actos oficiales, celebraciones multitudinarias y encuentros pastorales. El itinerario publicado por la Santa Sede se extenderá hasta el lunes 16 y llevará al pontífice por localidades de la costa, la sierra y la Amazonía. Entre los principales escenarios figuran el Estadio Nacional, las Pampas de Pimentel, Sacsayhuamán y la Base Aérea Las Palmas. Todos los horarios de las actividades en territorio peruano corresponden a la hora local. El viernes 13, León XIV saldrá del Callao a las 7:40 a. m. y llegará a Chiclayo a las 9:10 a. m. Su primera celebración será una misa en las Pampas de Pimentel, a las 10:30 a. m., seguida de una visita privada a la Capilla San Óscar A. Romero, a las 12:40 p. m. Durante la tarde se reunirá con representantes de la Iglesia en el Santuario de Nuestra Señora de la Paz, a las 4:30 p. m., y con el mundo universitario en la Universidad Católica Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo, a las 5:45 p. m. El sábado 14 iniciará sus actividades a las 8:00 a. m. con el rito de coronación de la Virgen Inmaculada en la Catedral de Santa María, en Chiclayo. Después viajará en helicóptero a Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, en Cajamarca, donde celebrará una misa a las 11:00 a. m. Tras regresar a Chiclayo, participará a las 5:30 p. m. en un encuentro de oración en Zaña, con motivo de la clausura del Año Jubilar de Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo. La agenda del domingo contempla dos destinos antes del retorno a Lima. El papa partirá de Chiclayo a las 7:50 a. m. y aterrizará en Cusco a las 10:00 a. m. A las 10:30 a. m. se encontrará con fieles y representantes de la piedad popular en el Parque Arqueológico Nacional de Sacsayhuamán. Posteriormente, a las 11:45 a. m., rezará el Ángelus en la plaza de la Catedral cusqueña. A la 1:05 p. m. saldrá hacia Pucallpa, donde su llegada está prevista para las 2:30 p. m. Media hora después se reunirá con misioneros, misioneras y representantes de los pueblos amazónicos en el Malecón Puerto Callao. La misa en la Villa Deportiva Regional Ucayali comenzará a las 4:45 p. m.; el vuelo de regreso a Lima despegará a las 7:05 p. m. y aterrizará a las 8:20 p. m. El último día de la visita comenzará a las 8:30 a. m. con un encuentro con el personal y las personas acogidas por las Hermanitas de los Ancianos Desamparados. A las 10:30 a. m., León XIV celebrará la misa en la Base Aérea Las Palmas, en Santiago de Surco. articles.title: Días no laborables por la visita del papa León XIV: cuándo serían y a quiénes alcanzarían
articles.summary: Visita del papa León XIV en Perú: ¿qué días serán no laborables en Lima, Callao, Chiclayo, Cusco y Pucallpa? El Gobierno peruano estableció días no laborables compensables en distintas regiones del país para facilitar el desplazamiento de la población y su participación en las actividades programadas por la visita del papa León XIV. Todos los detalles, en esta nota.
articles.body_text: Luego de que el Vaticano informara sobre la recuperación favorable del papa León XIV tras una intervención quirúrgica por un adenocarcinoma pulmonar, muchas instituciones y organizaciones continúan con la preparación para su visita al Perú. De hecho, el Gobierno nacional estima que la visita del Santo Padre al país podría movilizar a unas 854 000 personas, entre ellas más de 50 000 turistas extranjeros, quienes buscarán acercarse a él para recibir su bendición. Por ello, el Ejecutivo busca facilitar la participación de la población en las actividades que desarrollará el pontífice en las regiones que visitará, por lo que estableció días no laborables. Esta medida permitirá que los ciudadanos puedan asistir a los encuentros programados con Robert Prevost; sin embargo, las horas dejadas de trabajar deberán ser recuperadas posteriormente. En la siguiente nota te contamos todo lo que debes saber al respecto. A través del Decreto Supremo n.º 020-2026-TR, el Gobierno estableció días no laborables entre el 11 al 16 de noviembre para Lima, Callao, Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque, Piura, Cusco y Ucayali, con motivo a la visita del papa León XIV. Esta medida es compensable y se rige por normas distintas a las de los feriados. Es decir, en el sector público, las horas no laboradas deben recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores o en el plazo que establezca cada entidad. En tanto, en el sector privado, empleadores y trabajadores pueden acordar la forma de compensar esas horas. Si no llegan a un consenso, el empleador determina las condiciones para su recuperación. Por consiguiente, te presentamos, compartido por Infobae, los departamentos en las que regirá estos días de descanso: 11 de noviembre: 12 de noviembre: 13 de noviembre: 14 de noviembre: 15 de noviembre: 16 de noviembre: Durante su visita al Perú, el papa León XIV participará en una vigilia de oración junto a miles de jóvenes de entre 16 y 35 años, que se realizará el jueves 12 de noviembre, a las 6:00 p. m., en el Estadio Nacional. Asimismo, el lunes 16 presidirá la Santa Misa de clausura, programada para las 10:30 a. m. en la Base Aérea Las Palmas. Según los organizadores, los asistentes deberán contar con una entrada gratuita, que podrán obtener a través de las plataformas Teleticket y Ticketmaster. Sin embargo, quienes no puedan asistir a alguna de estas actividades por diversos motivos no podrán ceder su entrada a un familiar o ser querido, ya que los boletos son intransferibles y están vinculados a los datos personales registrados previamente por cada asistente, según informó el Arzobispado de Lima. Inclusive, indicaron que será indispensable presentar el documento de identidad en la puerta del recinto el día del evento, garantizando que el acceso sea gratuito.

El Gobierno peruano estableció días no laborables compensables en distintas regiones del país para facilitar el desplazamiento de la población y su participación en las actividades programadas por la visita del papa León XIV. Todos los detalles, en esta nota.
articles.body_text: Luego de que el Vaticano informara sobre la recuperación favorable del papa León XIV tras una intervención quirúrgica por un adenocarcinoma pulmonar, muchas instituciones y organizaciones continúan con la preparación para su visita al Perú. De hecho, el Gobierno nacional estima que la visita del Santo Padre al país podría movilizar a unas 854 000 personas, entre ellas más de 50 000 turistas extranjeros, quienes buscarán acercarse a él para recibir su bendición. Por ello, el Ejecutivo busca facilitar la participación de la población en las actividades que desarrollará el pontífice en las regiones que visitará, por lo que estableció días no laborables. Esta medida permitirá que los ciudadanos puedan asistir a los encuentros programados con Robert Prevost; sin embargo, las horas dejadas de trabajar deberán ser recuperadas posteriormente. En la siguiente nota te contamos todo lo que debes saber al respecto. A través del Decreto Supremo n.º 020-2026-TR, el Gobierno estableció días no laborables entre el 11 al 16 de noviembre para Lima, Callao, Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque, Piura, Cusco y Ucayali, con motivo a la visita del papa León XIV. Esta medida es compensable y se rige por normas distintas a las de los feriados. Es decir, en el sector público, las horas no laboradas deben recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores o en el plazo que establezca cada entidad. En tanto, en el sector privado, empleadores y trabajadores pueden acordar la forma de compensar esas horas. Si no llegan a un consenso, el empleador determina las condiciones para su recuperación. Por consiguiente, te presentamos, compartido por Infobae, los departamentos en las que regirá estos días de descanso: 11 de noviembre: 12 de noviembre: 13 de noviembre: 14 de noviembre: 15 de noviembre: 16 de noviembre: Durante su visita al Perú, el papa León XIV participará en una vigilia de oración junto a miles de jóvenes de entre 16 y 35 años, que se realizará el jueves 12 de noviembre, a las 6:00 p. m., en el Estadio Nacional. Asimismo, el lunes 16 presidirá la Santa Misa de clausura, programada para las 10:30 a. m. en la Base Aérea Las Palmas. Según los organizadores, los asistentes deberán contar con una entrada gratuita, que podrán obtener a través de las plataformas Teleticket y Ticketmaster. Sin embargo, quienes no puedan asistir a alguna de estas actividades por diversos motivos no podrán ceder su entrada a un familiar o ser querido, ya que los boletos son intransferibles y están vinculados a los datos personales registrados previamente por cada asistente, según informó el Arzobispado de Lima. articles.title: Perú-Petro y Pluspetrol cierran acuerdo que viabiliza tarifa promocional para la petroquímica: ¿que viene ahora?
articles.summary: El lote 88 tendrá regalías más flexibles para el gas destinado a la petroquímica. El Minem prepara decreto supremo para el nuevo pliego tarifario.
articles.body_text: El Ejecutivo desempolva el expediente de la petroquímica. Tras largos meses de abandono, el Ministerio de Energía y Minas (Minem) y Perú-Petro relanzan esta iniciativa, acariciada desde hace más de dos décadas por sucesivos gobiernos y devuelta al archivo por un sinnúmero de motivos, incluyendo la inercia gubernamental. “Estamos retomando el lanzamiento de la petroquímica porque no solamente debemos usar el gas natural para generación eléctrica, también debemos darle un valor agregado y es por eso que hemos reactivado las actividades pendientes de Perú-Petro, que estuvo negociando las regalías [para el proyecto] con el Consorcio Camisea”, indicó la viceministra de Hidrocarburos, Iris Cárdenas, en un reciente foro de energía. Ahora, la funcionaria acaba de anunciar que Perú-Petro ya “ha negociado y llegado a un acuerdo” que permitirá industrializar el gas y brindar, al mismo tiempo, seguridad alimentaria a nuestro país a través de la producción de fertilizantes. “Por eso, ya estamos elaborando el decreto supremo para que haya un pliego tarifario por redes de distribución con una tarifa especial para la petroquímica”, manifestó la funcionaria en el último Almuerzo Mensual de Compañías Operadoras Petroleras (Amecop). ¿De qué se trata esta tarifa especial? Hasta hace dos años había tres empresas interesadas en desarrollar un complejo petroquímico en el sur del Perú, entre ellas, la chilena Enaex. La iniciativa fracasó, empero, debido a la inoperancia del Gobierno en su propósito de facilitar el largo proceso, empezando por la implementación de una tarifa promocional para el gas natural destinado al proceso petroquímico. Y es que, como bien señala Luis Fernández, socio de Gas Energy, el gas para la petroquímica “siempre debe tener un precio especial”. “La principal razón es la competencia del gas natural abundante y barato que hay en Estados Unidos (…) Pero también el gas de Argentina, país que está trabajando en desarrollar más reservas y que tiene, además, el proyecto de desarrollar una nueva petroquímica en Bahía Blanca, que será una de las más grandes con las que cuentan”, explica el especialista. El gobierno de Javier Milei busca desarrollar, en efecto, la mayor planta de fertilizantes de la región, aprovechando las enormes reservas de ‘shale gas’ del yacimiento Vaca Muerta. Para competir contra este tipo de iniciativas y atraer, nuevamente, a los inversores petroquímicos, el Ejecutivo ha reemprendido la tarea de implementar la anhelada tarifa promocional para la petroquímica. En esa línea, Perú-Petro inició, semanas atrás, una serie de negociaciones con el Consorcio Camisea a fin de flexibilizar las regalías para el gas que se destinará al proyecto. Esto, para reducir el precio final de la molécula y posibilitar que la tarifa promocional sea la menor posible. Al respecto, dialogamos con el presidente de Perú-Petro, Esteban Bertarelli, a fines de setiembre, cuando las conversaciones venían tomando vuelo. “Estamos negociando con Pluspetrol (líder del consorcio) una modificación del contrato del lote 88 para poder tener una tarifa especial para la petroquímica”, refirió, precisando que las conversaciones iban por buen camino debido a “la buena voluntad” del consorcio negociador de la empresa. “Estamos, prácticamente, de acuerdo, y esperamos tener buenas noticias en las próximas semanas para que se fomente la petroquímica y se incremente el consumo de gas natural en el Perú, lo cual ayudaría a nuestra industrialización”, dijo entonces. Seis semanas después el acuerdo ya ha sido cerrado y, aunque no se conocen los detalles, se sabe que Perú-Petro ha fijado una regalía más baja sobre los volúmenes de gas que se orientarán a la petroquímica. Hablamos de entre 90 y 130 millones de pies cúbicos diarios del preciado hidrocarburo. Esto permitirá que Osinergmin y el Minem implementen una tarifa competitiva que vuelva a atraer a los inversionistas. Pero, ¿los habrá? “Todo el mundo habla de qué tan importante es tener una petroquímica propia para darle valor agregado al gas natural, pero no será tan fácil”, señala Fernández. Y es que, a entender del especialista, el precio de la molécula ha dejado de ser el factor crítico para gatillar el proyecto. Lo importante ahora, anota, es “conseguir al interesado”. “El precio de la molécula es importante, pero ningún interesado va a poner una inversión de US$1.500 millones o US$ 2.000 millones si no tiene un contrato de [suministro de gas] por, al menos, 20 años. Pero, ojo, son 20 años contados a partir del día en que la planta empieza a funcionar, lo cual ocurriría, en el mejor de los casos, en el 2030 o 2031”, estima. ¿Por qué habría problemas en garantizar 20 años de suministro de gas? El problema es que el contrato del lote 88, de donde provendrá el gas para la petroquímica, expira en el 2040, lo cual deja un margen pequeño, de 14 años, para que el Consorcio Camisea garantice el suministro de gas a los potenciales inversionistas. No es el Estado, en estos casos, quien garantiza la molécula de gas sino el productor, siempre y cuando pueda garantizar que está en condiciones de extraerlo por más de 20 años. Eso deja en el aire la pregunta de si el Gobierno renovará el contrato del lote 88 al Consorcio Camisea o buscará otro consorcio operador. “El tema es que la petroquímica se debió hacer cuando al consorcio le quedaban 20 años de contrato, pero no se hizo. Entonces, cualquier cosa que se piense hacer ahora tiene un grado de dificultad mayor. Nadie hace un proyecto para menos de 20 años”, enfatiza Fernández. ¿Qué planea hacer el Gobierno al respecto? Si desea que la petroquímica salga en el menor tiempo posible y no vuelva al archivo del olvido, debe tomar una decisión en el corto plazo. Este Diario se comunicó con Pluspetrol para obtener sus comentarios sobre las regalías negociadas con Perú-Petro, pero se excusó de responder.

articles.body_text: León XIV llegó al Perú este miércoles 11 de noviembre, a las 5:30 p. m., para comenzar una visita que combinará actos oficiales, celebraciones multitudinarias y encuentros pastorales. El itinerario publicado por la Santa Sede se extenderá hasta el lunes 16 y llevará al pontífice por localidades de la costa, la sierra y la Amazonía. Entre los principales escenarios figuran el Estadio Nacional, las Pampas de Pimentel, Sacsayhuamán y la Base Aérea Las Palmas. Su primera celebración será una misa en las Pampas de Pimentel, a las 10:30 a. m., seguida de una visita privada a la Capilla San Óscar A. Romero, a las 12:40 p. m. articles.title: Estados Unidos sigue contando votos: así avanza la nueva mayoría demócrata
articles.summary: Estados Unidos continúa el conteo de votos y avanza la definición de la nueva mayoría demócrata en el escenario político nacional.
articles.body_text: Estados Unidos sigue este viernes contando votos de las elecciones de medio mandato del pasado 3 de noviembre, aunque los resultados ya perfilan una amplia mayoría demócrata en ambas cámaras del Congreso y la recuperación del control de la mayoría de las gobernaciones por primera vez desde 2010. Los comicios, interpretados como un referéndum sobre la gestión del presidente, Donald Trump, se saldaron con una contundente victoria demócrata por el descontento ante el aumento en el coste de la vida y la impopular guerra contra Irán. El recuento continúa en varias contiendas, entre ellas las de Alaska para el Senado y la gobernación, donde todavía quedan votos por contabilizar y los resultados están pendientes de certificación. De los 435 escaños de la Cámara de Representantes, los demócratas han ganado ya 255, muy por encima de la mayoría de 218, frente a los 169 de los republicanos, mientras quedan 11 todavía por adjudicar. La oposición ha dado el vuelco a 44 escaños que estaban en manos de los republicanos, mientras que estos solo han arrebatado tres a los demócratas. Este resultado abre el camino para que el líder demócrata en la Cámara, Hakeem Jeffries, sea elegido en enero, cuando se constituya el nuevo Congreso, como el primer presidente afroamericano de la institución. Según el rastreo de Cook Political Report, a nivel nacional los demócratas lograron 66,2 millones de votos (56,2 %) frente a los 49,9 millones de los republicanos (42,4 %). Se trata de la victoria más amplia desde las elecciones de 1974, después de que el escándalo del Watergate derivara en la dimisión del presidente republicano Richard Nixon. En el Senado, donde se renovaba un tercio de sus 100 escaños, el bloque demócrata también ha conquistado la mayoría, con 55 puestos frente a los 44 republicanos, a la espera de que se resuelva la contienda en Alaska, donde la candidata demócrata encabeza el recuento. El Partido Demócrata ha arrebatado a los republicanos ocho escaños, algunos en bastiones que llevaban décadas o incluso cerca de un siglo sin elegir a un demócrata para el Senado: Carolina del Norte, Carolina del Sur, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Misisipi, Ohio y Texas. En este último estado, el senador electo James Talarico ha captado la atención nacional por su discurso progresista de inspiración cristiana. Los demócratas también han retenido el disputado escaño de Míchigan con la victoria de Abdul El-Sayed, que será el primer musulmán en ocupar un puesto en el Senado. En Alaska, donde ningún demócrata gana una elección al Senado desde 2008, Mary Peltola aventaja al senador republicano Dan Sullivan en unos 5.800 votos, con cerca del 88 % del voto escrutado. Los resultados sitúan a los demócratas en disposición de gobernar 29 de los 50 estados, frente a 20 de los republicanos, a la espera también de resolverse el resultado de Alaska. Será la primera vez desde 2010 que el partido controle la mayoría de las gobernaciones del país. De las 36 que estaban en juego, los demócratas han arrebatado cinco a los republicanos: Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio y Texas. Gina Hinojosa será la primera gobernadora latina de Texas, mientras que Keisha Lance Bottoms, ganadora en Georgia, será la primera mujer afroamericana en gobernar un estado de Estados Unidos. En Alaska, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins encabeza el recuento y, de confirmarse su victoria, será el primer demócrata en gobernar el estado desde 2002.

articles.title: Exclusive: This young startup wants to power floating data centers with the ocean’s heat, and investors are already on board | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Drogue is harvesting heat from the ocean to power data centers on floating vessels. The first prototype should be bobbing around the ocean, crunching bits, in less than two years.
articles.body_text: Anyone who has weathered a hurricane can tell you that the oceans — which fuel the storms — contain a tremendous amount of energy. Thanks to global warming, they’re holding more than ever. A new startup wants to harness that energy to power data centers. Drogue , which has kept a low profile until now, is building a system that harvests heat from the ocean to power data centers on board floating vessels. According to co-founder and CEO Sam Sipe, the first prototype should be bobbing around the ocean, crunching bits, less than two years from now. The goal, Sipe said, is to help data center developers deploy servers in AI-friendly timelines. “The data center industry is a real estate game, and so they’re playing on 8- to 10-year timelines, including interoperability with utilities and [independent system operators]” that manage regional power grids, he said. “AI demand has increased 10x in just the last three years. It’s completely incompatible.” Drogue was founded just six months ago in Washington, D.C., and the startup told TechCrunch exclusively that it has already raised $20 million, including from XYZ Venture Capital, Toyota Ventures, Tamarack Global, Dream, FDVC, Garuda Ventures, Flexcap, Boost VC, and Slow Ventures, among other investors. In those six months, Drogue has designed a multi-megawatt prototype that will be installed on a traditional oceangoing ship and sent out to sea in early 2028. Future versions will be built on floating structures that more closely resemble offshore oil platforms. To Sipe, the decision to turn to the ocean was obvious. After years flying E-2D Hawkeyes off U.S. Navy aircraft carriers, he had an appreciation for the ocean’s immense power. “Most people think, oh, ocean — hard waves, storms, corrosion, biofouling. And I just see this majestic place and resource that we just ignore,” he said. As the planet warms, the oceans have been absorbing an additional 5.8 million terawatt-hours of energy every year. By comparison, all of human civilization uses about 180,000 terawatt-hours each year. If Drogue were to take some, surely the ocean wouldn’t miss it. The startup’s technology works like a heat pump run in reverse. A heat pump uses electricity to move heat from one place to another; Drogue’s system instead uses a difference in temperature to generate electricity. This approach, known as ocean thermal energy conversion, or OTEC, was first developed in the 1950s. Surface waters are warmer, heated by the sun, while down-deep temperatures are much colder, about 39°F on average (4°C). “There’s basically no amount of heat we can pull out of that that will collapse that temperature differential,” Sipe said. To leverage the temperature differential, the startup’s system draws in warm surface water, uses it to cool the data centers, and then sends the now-warmer water to boil ammonia, a chemical that turns to gas at -28°F. That ammonia gas is then sent through a turbine to generate electricity. Once through the turbine, it courses through a condenser, which turns the gas back into a liquid. There, cold water drawn from 1,000 meters deep passes over the condenser’s fins to absorb the heat. The warmed water is then pumped back down to 1,000 meters, where it dissipates into the ocean. The ammonia gets sent back to the start of the sealed loop, and the cycle repeats.

articles.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation | TechCrunch

articles.body_text: Agent management startup LangChain has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation led by CapitalG, with participation from investors, including Singapore’s GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures, the company announced on Friday. That’s more than double its $1.25 billion valuation when it raised $125 million about a year ago , led by IVP. LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled the kinds of tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases. As the frontier AI labs delivered harnesses that now competently do those tasks, LangChain turned its focus toward managing AI agents. It has apparently found its stride in this highly competitive area with a simple message: letting businesses own their own intelligence. With its open source roots, the startup says its agent creation and management software, LangSmith, is not trying to lock users into any particular model, cloud, or ecosystem, unlike the major clouds or frontier AI labs. It also promises that LangSmith will contain agent behavior and is easy to use. True, there are plenty of other startups pitching similar advantages these days and also doing well ( case in point is newcomer Mintive ). However, LangChain has had a head start and now claims 7,000 LangSmith customers, including big-name startups like Harvey, Rippling, and Clay, and enterprises like Nvidia, Toyota, and Salesforce. articles.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China's most powerful AI models — uh oh, Jensen! | TechCrunch
articles.summary: New research shows the most advanced AI models from China were trained on banned Nvidia chips.
articles.body_text: The leading open-weight models developed by Chinese companies were trained on Nvidia chips that the U.S. government restricted from shipping to its largest geopolitical rival, a new research effort claims. The apparently widespread access to Blackwell GPUs among Chinese frontier labs shows the magnitude of the problem facing the leading chip designer. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company this week after admitting to his affair with Alice Huang, executive of Megaspeed, a company implicated in smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Alice Huang has also been alleged to be an agent of China’s intelligence service. While Jensen Huang’s relationships with a customer and two employees have drawn the most public interest, Nvidia’s potential corporate liability for export control violations likely factored into its decision to part ways with Huang. U.S. export controls are intended to protect the country’s leadership in AI capabilities against China, but Huang has long sought to open up that market. Blackwell GPUs are banned from export to China or Chinese-owned firms, while the Trump administration allows Nvidia to export the H200, a less powerful chip, provided shipments take a circuitous shipping route that allows the U.S. to claim a 25% tariff. Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher who leads the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs, analyzed the weights — the unique structure — of large language models released openly by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group. The weights still reflect the configurations of the chips used to train them, and DePue was able to find compelling evidence that the most closely watched models, including Moonshot’s Kimi’s K3 releases and DeepSeek’s V4 models, bear fingerprints from training on Blackwell chips. White House technology adviser Michael Kratsios said earlier this year that Moonshot had used export-banned Nvidia chips, citing U.S. intelligence sources. Epoch AI, a nonprofit research organization, estimates that about two million advanced chips entered China in 2024 and 2025 through schemes designed to hide their final destination. That doesn’t mean that these models were trained entirely on Nvidia chips, or that export control laws were necessarily violated; the chips could have been in an offshore data center, which has proven a popular way for Chinese firms to access compute and driven an industrial revolution in Malaysia. Epoch’s data estimates that 275,000 Nvidia AI accelerators were imported to Malaysia in 2024 and 2025. However, the ostensible goal of the export bans is to prevent exactly that: Chinese AI labs training on the most powerful chips. China hawks have long called for stronger controls on who uses chips, not just who owns them or where they are installed. “If we care about the U.S. tech edge, it doesn’t make any sense to me that you would not allow Chinese companies to access chips in mainland China or Hong Kong and Macau, but then say, actually, if you just go over to Malaysia, you can do whatever you want,” Sam Bresnick, a researcher at the Georgetown Center for Security and Emerging Technology, told TechCrunch this summer. Megaspeed, the company led by Alice Huang, has been at the center of that trade for several years through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, and has been the subject of investigations by both the U.S. and S i ngaporean government. Friday, Bloomberg also reported that a company with links to Alice Huang was involved in smuggling banned Nvidia chips to a data center in Shanghai. In May, the short-selling research firm Culper published a report arguing that Nvidia had a “ China problem ” because a significant share of its revenue was driven by Chinese demand, either through remote data centers or smuggling in violation of U.S. law. It detailed Megaspeed’s relationship with Nvidia and alleged that Alice Huang’s companies are backed by Chinese firms that are barred from accessing U.S. chips. Ironically, short-seller Culper’s bet against Nvidia wasn’t driven by the expectation of a U.S. government crackdown. Instead, it was focused on the Chinese government’s response to the bans, which was to recommit to its domestic chip industry.

articles.title: ChatGPT's new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you | TechCrunch
articles.summary: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out on users' behalf, starting with a limited rollout to U.S. Pro subscribers.
articles.body_text: OpenAI says that users are fully in control of the purchases, as they’re able to review the items, the total, and the payment card that will be used to complete the transaction before the checkout occurs. In addition, users will approve the purchases directly with a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint, which creates a record of their transaction. The addition comes as consumer-facing AI tools are working to find the right product-market fit, in terms of how they can help people be more efficient as they complete various tasks. While companies like DoorDash and Uber have so far reported low numbers of orders placed by AI agents, Meta’s Muse, which now has over 10 million users, has seen AI-assisted shopping become a top activity on its app. Other personal AI agents, like Instinct, also support making purchases on users’ behalf. It’s no surprise, then, that OpenAI would want to enter this space more with an agentic shopping feature of its own. The merchant will automatically receive what it needs to fulfill the order from the dot, like the shipping address and contact information, OpenAI says. The company notes that customers who shop via their dots will still be able to earn their credit card rewards and be able to take advantage of protections that typically come with cards, like being able to dispute transactions. The limited availability at launch will allow OpenAI to test and improve the feature and its capabilities before rolling it out more broadly. In the future, the company plans to offer users more control over the feature by allowing them to set spending limits or configure other parameters around purchase categories or time periods, so they can pre-approve purchases that their agent can then handle more autonomously. It also aims to make the agentic shopping feature an option at a broader number of supported retailers. This could be a challenge in some areas, where retailers are blocking AI agents from using their site ; on the shopping front, the largest retailer to ban AI agents is Amazon, as it aims to steer users to its own AI agent, Alexa, instead. To help retailers adapt to agentic commerce, OpenAI also published a Commerce Partner Playbook that offers tools and guidance to sites that want to support customers using agents. articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
articles.body_text: Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported. The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date. More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia. Bloomberg reported that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.” Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had been critical of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is said to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making. In a scathing letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) said they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy. “Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.

articles.title: Microsoft's latest email outage turned into a full-blown global cloud crisis | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Microsoft's day-long outage began with Outlook and Teams, and ended up taking much of the company's cloud services offline. Microsoft says it's gradually restoring service.
articles.body_text: Microsoft is slowly recovering from its daylong outage after much of the company’s systems were hit by a cascading software issue. The problems, which started Thursday, were initially flagged as affecting the company’s services in the U.S. and the Americas, but quickly spread around the world, as engineers struggled to recover downed servers. What began as an Outlook email and Teams video conferencing outage soon developed into a full-blown meltdown affecting the company’s cloud services for both consumer and business email, files, and documents. The outage also knocked out the company’s Copilot AI tools and Defender security screening software, and prevented system administrators from accessing their internal Intune dashboards and features. Some users reportedly experienced issues with accessing their cloud-based Windows computers. Microsoft hasn’t yet said what caused the issues, only saying the outage involved “a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable.” The company said it continues to investigate the cause. The outage affected a broad range of industries, including TechCrunch’s own email. We’ve reached out to Microsoft for comment about the incident. As of Friday morning on the U.S. East Coast, Microsoft’s Outlook email service had begun to recover and some emails have been trickling in. The recovery comes after engineers initially could not find the cause of the issue that was causing servers in Microsoft’s data centers to fail. Doug Madory, the director of internet analysis at Kentik, a company that monitors internet traffic worldwide, said in a post on Bluesky that traffic was returning to Microsoft’s services after about 18 hours of downtime. Microsoft said in its latest status update on Friday that there was “no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident,” and later noted that there was “not related to cyber or AI / agents.” That may be some solace for the millions who went without their email and online services yesterday, but the company is likely to face questions about its inability to swiftly recover from an outage of its own making. A Microsoft spokesperson did not respond to our questions asking if the company has the technical means to detect malicious activity, such as logs, or if Microsoft has a way to check what happened. “We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure,” said Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president for Copilot, agents, and platform, in a statement on Friday. “Our teams are reviewing what happened and how we can prevent similar issues going forward.” The last major incident affecting Microsoft services was in September , when a dayslong outage hit Microsoft’s cloud services. During that outage, Microsoft blamed a “core authentication configuration” issue that prevented users from accessing the service. This story was first published on November 12 and has been updated throughout.

articles.title: Israel's VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia's turmoil | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Given Nvidia’s stronghold on AI and its importance in Israel, many in the country's startup ecosystem are worried about the impact of his departure.
articles.body_text: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation has been received with worry in Israel, the company’s “second home,” as Huang described it in 2023. The company’s importance flows both ways, as the semiconductor giant has provided a major boost to Israel’s economic forecasts in recent years. Intel, Microsoft, and many homegrown startups also conduct a sizable share of their R&D in Israel. But owing to Nvidia’s stronghold on AI given the centrality of its GPUs for training LLMs and using them, many in the country are wondering how much of a reshuffle will result from the company’s leadership crisis. As with everything at Nvidia, Huang drove the company to acquire Israeli chipmaker Mellanox for $6.9 billion in 2019 and use the company as the base for its largest R&D facility outside of the U.S. Nvidia also made plans to build a multibillion-dollar campus in northern Israel. “Jensen brought Nvidia to Israel with the acquisition of Mellanox, so there is a strong positive sentiment towards Nvidia and Jensen in Israel’s tech community,” Israeli repeat cybersecurity entrepreneur Pavel Gurvich told TechCrunch. Beyond the 6,000 locals Nvidia employs, the bigger question is whether the company will remain as committed to Israel with someone else at the helm. As a result, his line of succession is being observed just as closely by those who hope the company continues to do so as by those who don’t want it to happen. The latter have already gathered that they may be in for disappointment. In a 2023 interview that is now doing the rounds on X, interim CEO Colette Kress had declared that as Nvidia’s CFO, she typically started her day “with Israel meetings, and only then continue[d] to California.” Kress may not remain in charge in the long run, but the many names floated for the role include two Israelis , Apple’s Johny Srouji and Nvidia’s Michael Kagan — although they’re not at the top of the still quite tentative list . Regardless of who gets chosen, Huang’s successor will likely have less of a grip on Nvidia and the tech industry as a whole. But investors don’t think that would cause demand for Nvidia’s product to fade away. According to Yanai Oron, a general partner at Vertex Ventures Israel, “slower decisions at Nvidia could give competitors an opening, but if that uncertainty also slows AI spending, they could end up with a bigger share of a smaller opportunity.” Nvidia has been responsible for a vast share of the spending in the global AI industry. Under Huang’s leadership, the company used its cash reserves to massively invest across the spectrum, both in companies and in its own next-generation chips . Such an empire may not be doomed to fall with its architect’s ouster, but it does seem less likely to become a full-on monopoly. According to Adi Levanon, a founder and managing partner at Selah Ventures, “[Huang’s] departure doesn’t dismantle Nvidia’s technology or ecosystem, but it could give competitors more room to shape what comes next.” And now that companies globally are deploying increasingly demanding AI agents into their workflows, there’s been a lot of interest — and some venture capital — flowing into developers of AI-specific chips and inference software that could compete with Nvidia’s.

articles.title: Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang's 'scheme' with Trump | TechCrunch
articles.summary: This Congressional investigation into Nvidia's China sales and its dealings with Trump is the second one, so far, since news of the alleged spy affair broke.
articles.body_text: Democrats on Thursday opened an inquiry into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China. Earlier on Thursday, the company ousted its CEO Jensen Huang . He also agreed to testify to a different set of Republican-led Congressional committees. Huang was removed from the company he founded after he confessed to an extramarital affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. (He has since been accused of having more affairs , with Nvidia employees.) The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that U.S. officials suspect of helping route advanced Nvidia chips into China. The Democratic inquiry comes from Rep. Richard Neal (D-Mass.), the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, and Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee. As the minority party, they can ask questions but can’t compel answers. Their humdinger of a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asks the department to preserve records about an arrangement they find questionable and, they allege, illegal. “The scheme worked like this,” as the letter describes it. President Trump agreed to sales of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China as long as the chips, manufactured by Taiwan, were first shipped to the United States. On arriving, Trump added a tariff “effectively taking a cut of Nvidia’s sales to China through what appears to be an unconstitutional export tax system,” the letter said. Then the Commerce Department, under Lutnick, issued an export license. By the way, the deal between Trump and Nvidia to share revenue was public. In August 2025, Nvidia and AMD both agreed to share 15% of their revenue from chip sales to China with the U.S. government as part of a deal to secure export licenses, the AP reported at the time. But the letter questions why Lutnick continued to allow Megaspeed to buy chips even after he was reportedly informed by U.S. intelligence of their suspicions of Alice Huang and of Jensen Huang’s relationship with her. It questions why the department reportedly green-lit other Asian companies to buy Nvidia chips “with no physical presence at their listed addresses.” So the inquiry is aimed at the administration, not just at Nvidia and Huang. The letter also questions how Nvidia’s donations to Trump’s projects factored in. It notes that the export deal was approved after Trump learned of “Mr. Huang’s compromised position” in sleeping with an alleged spy, and after Nvidia donated $26 million toward Trump’s projects, including the ballroom. It appears to be asking if Trump used his knowledge of the affair to secure donations from Nvidia. Interestingly, in a “60 Minutes” interview with President Trump that aired on Sunday, Trump mentioned how he and his team had threatened an unnamed AI exec with jail , and after that, the exec “totally changed.” This Congressional investigation into Nvidia’s China sales and its dealings with Trump is the second one, so far, since news of the alleged spy affair broke. The Republican-led group involves leaders from the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the House Intelligence Committee. That group has demanded that Huang come to them and testify in a closed-door session. They had threatened to subpoena him if he didn’t voluntarily agree. articles.title: Hugging Face CEO vows to keep fighting for open source AI after Jensen Huang's exit | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Hugging Face's CEO pledged to keep fighting for open source AI after Huang's exit, raising questions about Nvidia's $12.9 billion acquisition.
articles.body_text: Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue briefly commented on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday, calling it a “really sad day.” Nvidia had announced its plan to acquire the platform for open source AI models in September for $12.9 billion, making it the second-largest acquisition in the company’s history, just behind that of chipmaker Groq’s assets for $20 billion in December 2025. “This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!,” Delangue wrote on X. This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go! The post is interesting as it implies that Huang’s departure is potentially worrying to open source advocates, and he’s attempting to offer reassurance. As Nvidia’s CEO, Huang was known as a strong advocate for open source AI and open-weight models, which is why there could be concerns about how a company that’s no longer under his leadership will now approach this space. After Nvidia announced its plans to acquire Hugging Face, the U.S. Department of Justice began making inquiries about how the deal would impact competition in the AI market, Reuters reported in October . While Nvidia pledged that the platform would preserve open support, it would also allow the company to control a major distribution channel for AI models. The Hugging Face deal is still scheduled to close in the first half of 2027. Requests for further comment on the deal status and whether Hugging Face has spoken yet with Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress were not returned. Huang’s advocacy for open source and open-weight AI has long extended beyond Hugging Face. In July, the CEO published an AI policy letter as his first-ever post on the social network X . The letter, which was signed by 25 companies, including Microsoft, Meta, Hugging Face, IBM, Palantir, and others, urged the U.S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models. It said models that “anyone can download, inspect, modify, and run on their own infrastructure” are an important part of the AI ecosystem because they make AI “more accessible, adaptable, and widely available.” Huang also wrote that open-weight models expand access to the AI economy, strengthen competition, and give customers greater control, as they know they won’t become locked into a single provider. “Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty,” his post on X stated. For my first post, I’m sharing a letter @NVIDIA signed on why open models matter. AI will transform every industry, power every company, and be built by every country. Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty.… pic.twitter.com/t02bi51N4C In August, Nvidia also announced a $6 billion deal with the coding startup Poolside to help build out an open AI ecosystem in the U.S. to help the country compete against Chinese companies like DeepSeek and Kimi K3, The Wall Street Journal reported at the time. Last month, Nvidia expanded its Nemotron family of open-weight models with a large 120-billion-parameter model for agents used by the enterprise as well as with two new lightweight Bolt models that run on PCs. Earlier this year, Huang promoted open source AI during his January keynote address at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, noting that open source models have “really revolutionized artificial intelligence.”

FAA ger inga ytterliga uppgifter, men skriver att ”samtliga avgående flygningar ska hållas kvar på marken tills vidare”. ”Avgående flyg ska stanna på marken tills vidare. Ankommande internationella flygningar kommer att hanteras från fall till fall” , skriver myndigheten. ABC News rapporterar att FAA:s beslut beror på något slags kommunikationsproblem. Exakt vad är ännu oklart. FAA stoppade flygtrafiken i Chicago på grund av kommunikationsproblem kort innan man beslöt att stoppa flygtrafiken i hela landet. USA:s transportminister Sean Duffy bekräftar i sociala medier att flygstoppet beror på ett kommunikationsproblem som påverkar flygledningen. Enligt Duffy har alla flygledningscentraler drabbats av problemet. Tekniker arbetar med att utreda orsaken. Den här typen av rikstäckande flygstopp är mycket ovanliga i USA. Senaste ett sådant infördes var i januari 2023 då ett system för att informera piloter slutade fungera, rapporterar Sky News. Trumpadministrationen vill modernisera gamla kommunikationssystem inom flygledningen. Så sent som i dag bad Vita huset kongressen om ytterligare miljardanslag, drygt 30 miljarder dollar, för att uppgradera flygplatserna och flyglandningssystemen, skriver Sky News.
